help.intro: A radio quiz of about two minutes: the host describes two famous people from German history, step by step, from appearance to character to life, and a listener on the phone has to guess who they are. The first is a man with wild white hair who did not like socks and changed physics; the second is a woman from Berlin who became a film star in Hollywood and refused to come home. The quiz is invented; the facts about the two people are real and were checked. You hear what you have just learnt: describing people (Er hat lange, weiße Haare. Sie ist groß und schlank. Er ist freundlich, aber ein bisschen chaotisch) and reflexive verbs (sich interessieren für, sich erinnern an, sich freuen über, sich ärgern, sich kämmen). Listen once for the whole quiz, then once for each clue.
help.tips[0].title: Describing a person
help.tips[0].text: Appearance: Er ist groß / klein, schlank / kräftig. Sie hat lange, blonde Haare und blaue Augen. Er trägt eine Brille, einen Schnurrbart (moustache), einen Hut. Age: Er ist etwa fünfzig. Character: freundlich, ruhig, lustig, ernst, chaotisch, mutig (brave), stur (stubborn), klug (clever). Comparisons help: Sie sieht aus wie …; Er wirkt (seems) müde. Adjective after sein: no ending; before a noun: with ending (lange Haare, ein weißer Schnurrbart).
help.tips[0].examples[0].en: He has wild white hair and a moustache, wears old jumpers and always looks a little chaotic.
help.tips[0].examples[1].en: She is tall and slim, has blonde hair and a deep voice; she seems cool, but she is very brave.
help.tips[0].check.why: tragen = to wear; eine Brille is singular for one pair of glasses.
help.tips[1].title: Reflexive verbs
help.tips[1].text: Some verbs come with mich / dich / sich / uns / euch: sich interessieren für (to be interested in), sich erinnern an (to remember), sich freuen über / auf (to be glad about / look forward to), sich ärgern über (to be annoyed about), sich kämmen (to comb one's hair), sich konzentrieren auf, sich verlieben in (to fall in love with), sich weigern (to refuse). Forms: ich interessiere mich, du interessierst dich, er/sie interessiert sich, wir interessieren uns, ihr interessiert euch, sie/Sie interessieren sich. With the Perfekt: Sie hat sich geweigert.
help.tips[1].examples[0].en: He was interested only in physics and never combed his hair.
help.tips[1].examples[1].en: She refused to come back to Germany, and the Germans were annoyed about it.
help.tips[1].check.q: Wir ____ ____ an die alten Filme. (sich erinnern)
help.tips[1].check.why: wir takes the reflexive pronoun uns: wir erinnern uns.
help.remember[0]: Er hat weiße Haare, trägt eine Brille, ist klug und chaotisch; adjective after sein without ending.
help.remember[1]: sich interessieren für, sich erinnern an, sich freuen über, sich ärgern über, sich weigern: mich, dich, sich, uns, euch.
help.exam: Quiz shows or interviews in which a person is described and has to be recognised are a typical listening task at this level.
help.hook: Wild white hair and no socks; a deep voice and a refusal to come home: listen to two famous Germans being described and guess who they are.
help.vocab[5].example: Hosen und Frack, das ist damals ein Skandal.
passageTranslation:
Host: Welcome to 'Who am I?'. On the phone is Ms Kaya from Hannover. I describe a famous person, and you guess. Ready?
Listener: Ready!
Host: First person. It is a man. He is not very tall, has wild white hair and a moustache. He wears old jumpers and never puts on socks, not even for important appointments. He always looks a little chaotic.
Listener: Hm, an artist?
Host: No. He is interested in physics, already as a child. At school he is good, but he gets annoyed about the strict teachers. Later he works in an office in Bern and on the side writes texts that change physics completely. He likes playing the violin and sailing, but he cannot swim.
Listener: White hair, physics, violin … That is Albert Einstein!
Host: Right! Born 1879 in Ulm. In 1921 he gets the Nobel Prize, in 1933 he leaves Germany for ever and lives in the USA. He says: I have no special talent, I am only passionately curious. Second person. It is a woman. She is tall and slim, has blonde hair, long legs and a deep voice. She often wears trousers and a tailcoat, which is a scandal at the time.
Listener: An actress?
Host: Yes. She comes from Berlin, from Schöneberg. In 1930 she goes to Hollywood and becomes a world star. She refuses to come back to Germany in the Nazi era and sings instead for the American soldiers. Many Germans are annoyed about it for years. All her life she remembers Berlin and sings: I still have a suitcase in Berlin.
Listener: That is Marlene Dietrich!
Host: Right again! Born 1901, died 1992 in Paris. She is buried in Berlin, in Schöneberg, not far from the house where she was born. Ms Kaya, you have two out of two. Congratulations, you win the books of the week!
Listener: I am very happy! Thank you!

questions[5].questionTranslation: 'She refuses to come back to Germany in the Nazi era.' What does sich weigern mean?
